items.text: Bring your valid provisional (or full) driving licence photocard
items.note: Without it, the test usually can't go ahead, even if the rest of your paperwork is in order.

items.text: Bring glasses or contact lenses if you need them to meet the eyesight standard
items.note: If you normally wear them to drive, you must wear them for the eyesight check and the rest of the test.

items.text: Your car is insured for the test, taxed, and has a valid MOT if it needs one
items.note: The examiner can refuse to conduct the test in a vehicle that isn't legally roadworthy.

items.text: L plates (D plates in Wales) are displayed correctly on the front and back
items.note: Required right up until you pass — remove them once you've got your result, not before.

items.text: You know the location of the main controls and can perform basic safety checks
items.note: You don't need to have learned in this exact car, but you should be comfortable with it.

section: At the start of the test

items.text: Eyesight check — read a number plate from 20 metres away
items.note: If you can't read it (even with glasses or contacts), the test ends immediately without going any further.

items.text: One 'tell me' vehicle safety question, asked before you set off
items.note: For example, how you'd check the brakes are working. Practise these in the Show Me Tell Me flashcards.

items.text: General driving ability across a range of road types and traffic conditions
items.note: This is the bulk of the test — normal driving, junctions, roundabouts, lane discipline, and reacting appropriately throughout.

items.text: One 'show me' vehicle safety question, asked while you're driving
items.note: For example, being asked to use the heated rear window demister while safe to do so.
Following directions from a sat nav, a series of traffic signs, or a combination of both — the examiner will explain which.

items.text: One manoeuvre, chosen by the examiner on the day
items.note: Usually one of: parallel park at the side of the road, park in a bay (driving in or reversing in), or pull up on the right, reverse about two car lengths, and rejoin traffic.
Not asked in every test, but be ready for it throughout — the examiner will give a clear signal when it's time.

items.text: Pass with zero serious or dangerous faults, and generally no more than 15 minor driving faults
items.note: A single serious or dangerous fault fails the test outright, even with an otherwise clean drive — minor faults only add up if the same one keeps repeating or several accumulate.
